# `silk/machine/definition`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The whole chart as data: a `Definition` can be written to JSON and read back, so external
tools can show a machine, and a build step can generate Silk source from one.

## Details
A definition is text all the way down. The effects a row leaves, and the value a transition
enters, are written as a program writes them, such as `Exits { status: 4 }`. A guard is its
name, when it has one.

## Gotchas
A value is written from its unions, enums, structs, numbers, booleans and text. A field of
another type, such as a list, is written as `..`.

Import as `Definition` with `import silk.machine.definition { Definition }`.

Public declarations: 12.

<a id="Definition"></a>

## `Definition`

```silk
pub struct Definition
```

A machine: its chart and the charts of every region below it, each one time.

The charts are a flat list and a region names its chart, so a chart that several states
hold as a region is written one time. The first chart is the machine's own.

<a id="Definition.name"></a>

### Field `name`

```silk
pub name: String
```

<a id="Definition.charts"></a>

### Field `charts`

```silk
pub charts: List<ChartDefinition>
```

<a id="Values.impl.write"></a>

### Associated function `write`

```silk
pub effect fn write<T>(value: &T, text: &mut String) -> ()
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Appends `value` to `text` as a program writes it: `Exits { status: 4 }` for a variant of
a union, `Archive` for a member of an enum, `Point { x: 1, y: 2 }` for a struct, and the
digits or the word for a number or a boolean. Text is written in double quotes without
escapes. A field of any other type, such as a list, is written as `..`.
